clue.text: Stop that raucous laughter and come to the point

definitions.meaning: cackle is loud harsh laughter, and to cut it is to silence it
the idiom means stop the idle chatter and get down to business

explanation.surface: An exasperated host silences the noisy guffawing and demands that everyone get on with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: the literal sense ends noisy cackling, and the idiom means dropping small talk for the matter in hand.

clue.text: We entered disheartened and shrank back

indicators.note: one piece has entered, gone inside, the other

parts.note: an apple with its heart, the core, removed is cored
taken as written

explanation.surface: We came in dispirited and recoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' reads as gloomy, but it is literal: with the heart taken out, CORED.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to cringe or recoil in fear.

clue.text: Arrange no truce!

indicators.note: to arrange letters is to put them in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A commander's order that there be no ceasefire.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowing no truce means beating the enemy soundly, which is to thrash them.

clue.text: Execute by gibbet and bullet, and wait to see the outcome

parts.note: to kill on a gallows is to hang
a round is a single cartridge or bullet

explanation.surface: A grim choice of execution methods, then a patient pause for the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger, idling about until something happens, is a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Ciphers Desmond is given by regimental commander

parts.note: CO stands for Commanding Officer
Des is the short form of the name Desmond

explanation.surface: A colonel hands secret ciphers to a soldier called Desmond.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciphers and codes are both systems for disguising messages.

clue.text: He tells how to dismiss an officer

definitions.meaning: a bank teller who pays out money
to discharge a commissioned officer in disgrace from the forces

explanation.surface: Someone explains the procedure for sacking a military officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a bank clerk handling money, and the military verb for dishonourable discharge.

clue.text: Left breadwinner to become a student

parts.note: the person who brings in the household income is the earner

explanation.surface: A family's provider quits work to go back to college.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone being taught, a pupil.

clue.text: Traveller's joy is freshly-cooked almond breads

indicators.note: cooking the words afresh remakes their letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe blurb: the joy of a journey is newly baked almond loaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Traveller's joy is the wild clematis, whose fluffy seed heads give it its other common name.
explanation.definitionFit: Traveller's joy and the bearded name are two common names for the same wild clematis plant.

clue.text: Doubly depressed when given the information

parts.note: two words each meaning depressed: low, then down
two words each meaning depressed: low, then down

explanation.surface: Someone feels twice as gloomy on hearing the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: The low-down is informal for the inside facts or full details.

clue.text: I had retired workers employed in spinning

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
the employees of a firm are its staff

explanation.surface: Someone once had employees who have now retired, all working in a spinning mill.
explanation.definitionFit: A distaff is the stick that holds wool or flax for hand spinning.

clue.text: Seats only need be paid for if unfitted

definitions.text: Seats only need be paid for if unfitted

parts.words: Seats only need be paid for if unfitted
parts.note: if only seats carry a charge, places where you stand cost nothing; also furniture not built in

explanation.surface: A theatre pricing rule: pay only for a seat if you are unfitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase in two halves: with only seats charged, standing is free; and the joined term means not built in.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture not fixed to a wall or built into a room stands on its own.

clue.text: Sailor sent on a mission to Mars and Venus

definitions.text: sent on a mission to Mars and Venus
definitions.meaning: NASA's series of planetary space probes of the 1960s and 1970s bore this name

explanation.surface: A seaman is despatched on an interplanetary voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a seaman, and the name of NASA's early probes to the inner planets.

clue.text: Elegant girl initially goes to the north-east clad in French silk

indicators.note: one piece is dressed in, wrapped round by, the other

parts.note: soie is the French word for silk

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of girl

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A stylish young woman heads north-east wearing French silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Soignée describes a woman who is well groomed and sophisticated.

clue.text: For instance, debt-collector returned to give a prod

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
a dun is one who demands payment of a debt

explanation.surface: A debt-collector came back to give a reluctant payer a poke.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge is to push gently, especially with the elbow.

clue.text: Where crutches are held in readiness for action

definitions.meaning: crutches are tucked into the armpits

explanation.surface: Someone describes where walking aids go, then turns to troops prepared for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: the armpit area, and the phrase meaning mobilised and armed.

clue.text: One who recklessly challenged iniquity

parts.note: to have dared someone is to have challenged them
evil is wickedness, iniquity

explanation.surface: A reckless hero who took on wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is a person who takes wild risks, defying danger.

clue.text: Lawyers offer to get a local assistant

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers
to tender is to offer, as a bid

explanation.surface: Lawyers make a bid to hire a helper in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for one's nearby pub, so 'local assistant' is a pub worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone serving drinks behind the counter is a helper at the pub.

clue.text: Find a substitute for two fabrics

parts.note: rep is a ribbed cloth
lace is an openwork fabric

explanation.surface: A tailor seeks alternatives to a pair of cloths.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace something is to put another in its stead.

clue.text: Former noble title that is given by right

parts.note: earl is a rank of the peerage
IE abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's previous title is bestowed by entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Former and earlier both mean preceding in time.

clue.text: Country melodies on reflection have variable content

indicators.note: the second piece is the contents held inside the first
reflection turns the word back, as in a mirror

parts.note: airs are tunes or melodies
Y is a mathematician's unknown variable

explanation.surface: Folk tunes, thought over, prove to be of mixed quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: Underclothing for the semi-sober

parts.note: a teetotaller is TT, so one only half sober has just one of the two Ts

explanation.surface: A garment designed for someone only half off the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: TT means teetotal; half of it is a lone T, which with a word for lone gives a vest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless vest worn under a shirt or for athletics.

clue.text: All change! Their vocational courses?

parts.note: the railway call to switch carriages, read as people being taught a new skill

explanation.surface: A guard's announcement on a train, followed by a question about job training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All change' is the cry at a terminus when passengers must leave the train; read as wordplay it suggests a train once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taught a new trade or skill.

clue.text: A place to store trim clothes

indicators.note: one piece holds the other in store inside it

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
to pare is to trim

explanation.surface: Somewhere to keep neat garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for garments.

clue.text: Ease off when the lease has expired

definitions.meaning: a property let that is finished, its term up

explanation.surface: Advice to relax once a rental agreement has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a slackening, and a tenancy whose term has run out.

clue.text: Not indeed indicated

indicators.note: the first word is placed inside the second

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flat denial: not so, indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' looks like one emphatic word but splits into 'in' plus DEED, with NOT going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to signify or point out.

clue.text: A writer for The Times and Daily Recorder

definitions.meaning: someone who writes down the times of events, not a newspaper journalist
a person who logs each day's events

explanation.surface: A journalist on a national paper and on a daily news title.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: one who keeps a journal records each day's happenings.

clue.text: Conceited, inwardly sick and criminal

indicators.note: inwardly means placed within the other word

parts.note: vain means conceited
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A description of someone arrogant, unwell and law-breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wrongdoer, a crook.

clue.text: Optional term used for an orthodox high churchman

indicators.note: the letters are used, made over, in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A word chosen at will for a senior Orthodox cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Orthodox Church a metropolitan is a bishop ranking above ordinary bishops, heading a province.
